name.text: Probabilities from a sample space grid

questiontext.text:
[[if test="is(s=6)"]]

Two fair dice, one red and one blue, are rolled and the two numbers are [[if test="is(op=0)"]]added[[else]]multiplied[[/if]] to give a score.

[[else]]

A fair die is rolled and a fair spinner with \({@s@}\) equal sectors numbered 1 to \({@s@}\) is spun. The two numbers are [[if test="is(op=0)"]]added[[else]]multiplied[[/if]] to give a score.

[[/if]]

You may find a grid helpful.

Give each probability exactly, as a fraction or an exact decimal.

(a) How many equally likely outcomes are there?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find \(P(\text{score} = {@k@})\).

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(c) Find \(P(\text{score greater than } {@m@})\).

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:

The grid shows the score for each one; the scores equal to \({@k@}\) are in brackets and shaded.

(b) \({@ck@}\) of the \({@n@}\) cells have score \({@k@}\), so \(P(\text{score} = {@k@}) = \dfrac{{@ck@}}{{@n@}} = {@ta2@}\). The \({@nd@}\) different scores are not equally likely: count cells, not scores.

(c) \({@cg@}\) cells have a score greater than \({@m@}\) (the score \({@m@}\) itself is left out), so \(P(\text{score greater than } {@m@}) = \dfrac{{@cg@}}{{@n@}} = {@ta3@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Probability III: probabilities from a sample space grid

Grade 12 CBE Essential 3.2: Count the outcomes of two experiments as a product and find probabilities of scores by counting cells of a grid.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 5, Section A, questions A1 and A2 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Foundation 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: sums and products of a die and a second die or spinner, randomised, with new questions and numbers.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: You added. Each of the 6 outcomes of the [[if test="is(s=6)"]]red die[[else]]die[[/if]] goes with each of the \({@s@}\) outcomes of the [[if test="is(s=6)"]]blue die[[else]]spinner[[/if]], so the two numbers of outcomes are multiplied, not added.

falsefeedback.text: Draw a grid: 6 rows and \({@s@}\) columns. How many cells are there?

truefeedback.text: Your value is close to the right one but has been rounded. Give the exact probability as a fraction or an exact decimal.
There are \({@nd@}\) different scores, but they are not equally likely. Count the cells of the grid with score \({@k@}\).
You divided by \({@6+s@}\), which is \(6 + {@s@}\). The equally likely outcomes are the cells of the grid, with 6 rows and \({@s@}\) columns: divide by the number of cells.
A probability is always between 0 and 1, so \({@ans2@}\) cannot be a probability.

falsefeedback.text: Count the cells with score \({@k@}\) and divide by \({@n@}\).

truefeedback.text: Your value is close to the right one but has been rounded. Give the exact probability as a fraction or an exact decimal.
You included the score \({@m@}\). Greater than \({@m@}\) leaves it out.
You divided by \({@6+s@}\), which is \(6 + {@s@}\). The equally likely outcomes are the cells of the grid, with 6 rows and \({@s@}\) columns: divide by the number of cells.
A probability is always between 0 and 1, so \({@ans3@}\) cannot be a probability.

falsefeedback.text: Count the cells with a score greater than \({@m@}\) and divide by \({@n@}\).
